Repair the Reynolds Kit Car by finding some wrecks.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The GTA 6 Kit Car locations are spread all over Leonida, making your search to repair Wyman's fourth car significantly more involved than the Transgressor, Riata, or even the Mamba GT. There are five whole cars to scan with the WAiNK It app, but it's well worth it, because the Kit Car is super fast and stylish.

It's worth noting that you'll need to complete the Chapter 3 mission, Meet the Heders, to acquire the cut-off tool (since one of the Kit Cars is in a locked shipping container). After the Kit Car, there's one additional vehicle in the Classic Car Collection, the Deviant, but it doesn't actually require a collectible hunt as Wyman will simply offer it to you, making this your last one.

The first Kit Car is inside the garage at Willie's Service Center in south Vice City, southeast of Salton, and northwest of Tequesta. Just north of the purchasable 7th Avenue Garage and west of Vice City Firearms,you'll spot a building on the left labelled as Willie's Service Center with a brown top half and blue lower half.

Enter the ground floor via the door around the left side by the stairs. You'll have to break in, which sounds an alarm, so be quick scanning the car inside.

The second one is on Casanova Island, the rightmost of the Rialto Islands that connect west Vice City with east Vice City. When you reach the island, driving west to east (coming from Vespucci) head along the northernmost road and look to your left about halfway across the island for a big white villa with a small gated garage next door—it's next to a big vacant lot. Push the gate open to find the kit car right in front of you.

The third one is in a shipping container on Wild Hog Point, directly to the southwest of Port Gellhorn, on the big peninsula that sticks out where the airfield is located. For this one, you'll need to have completed the Meet the Heders mission in Chapter 3 to acquire the cut-off tool to open it.

It's on the westernmost edge of the point, around the middle of the pools that look a bit like a seahorse on the map. Due to the end of Chapter 2, similar to Grassrivers, this area is also a hot spot for police, so be careful while driving around. Look for the yellow scoop container, crack it open, and scan the car inside.

The fourth one is around the back of Donnie's Auto Repair Watson Bay in Watson Bay town, west of Hamlet, southwest of Port Gellhorn. This garage (which has Donnie's Auto Repair written on it) is next door to the Pay 'n' Spray - Watson Bay. Just head around the left side of the building and you'll find the Kit Car to scan immediately on your right.

The fifth Kit Car is in a fancy garage on the west side of Capri on the little curving northern peninsula of houses. Capri is south of Port Gellhorn on the coast. Drive along the road until you spot the building site on your right and the green villa on your left—just after it, you'll find the driveway of the house you want, also on the left. Follow the path and break into the garage on your right to find the car.

Same as always, wait for Wyman to finish the car and call, then click the payment request he sends in his following text to Buck him $1,500 before collecting the car from the nav point at his scrapyard.

This is actually the final car hunt, as later Wyman will call you and straight-up ask if you want the final car, a Deviant. You then pay him $1,000 for labour, and it's immediately yours to collect, so with this, you've basically finished the Classic Car Collection.

#3651. So Is The $100 GTA 6 Ultimate Edition Actually Worth It?

Before Grand Theft Auto 6 even launched, there was some controversy online over the announcement of a $100 “Ultimate Edition” version of the game that would include access to a few exclusive shops and in-game cosmetics. So, now that GTA 6 is here and I’ve spent over 150 hours with it, I can share what’s in the Ultimate Edition, how you access this stuff, and if it’s worth upgrading from the standard $80 version of GTA 6. The short version is…eh, probably not.

In GTA 6, there are five stores that are locked behind the Ultimate Edition paywall. These stores include an exclusive tattoo parlor, street clothing shop, and hair salon. Now, at first, I thought it was pretty shitty of Rockstar to hide stores behind a paywall. And to be clear, it still does suck that a few shops are only accessible if you pay $20 more. But after playing GTA 6, I discovered that the world is filled with over 600 stores. There are already so many clothing, car, hair, make-up, and nail options in the base game. So the Ultimate Edition’s extra few stores don’t feel that necessary. And after actually visiting these shops and seeing what they have to offer, I don’t think people are missing out on that much.

First up, there’s 305, a clothing store specializing in urban, skater-inspired clothing and gear. There’s some alright stuff in here, including some nice-looking jeans for Jason and a cool graphic shirt or two. And a really wild fuzzy hat for Lucia. But the options in here aren’t something you need to have. You can create plenty of great and cool outfits without stopping by this Ultimate Editionâonly retailer.

Next up is the tattoo shop Electric Fang. Of all the Ultimate Edition stores, this is the coolest one to enter. And I do think some of Electric Fang’s tat designs are solid. But again, there are so many other options in the game for ink that I’m not sure these are very necessary or worth the $20 upgrade.

Sara’s Unisex Salon might be the best of the bunch as it offers some stylish hairdos for both Jason and Lucia. But on top of that, it offers some really nice makeup options for Lucia and cool nail art, too. I ended up using some of these options during my time as Lucia because I liked them so much. Still, again, there are so many other good options for haircuts and nail art already in GTA 6 that I’m not sure you need to spend $20 more on this version.

There are also two exclusive car mod garages in GTA 6‘s Ultimate Edition. One of them, Rideout Customs, offers some really gaudy and exotic paint and accessories options. If you wanted a neon-pink car with stripes painted to look like cheetah print, well, this is the place for you.

The other mod shop, One-Eyed Willie’s, is more useful. It offers up some really nice off-road options. There aren’t nearly as many off-road modding options in GTA 6 as there are for street cars, so losing out on access to this in the base game is a shame. I also love that One-Eyed Willie’s offers up a random paint job for every car in the game, including non-off-road vehicles, that you can only see once it’s applied. I brought my Banshee into the shop, and it received this pretty pink design that I loved.

The Ultimate Edition also includes some unique free clothing items based on characters from an in-universe cartoon you can watch. These clothes are fine. I guess if you like the show a lot, they might be fun to wear. But…eh.

Beyond the stores and cosmetics, there are some exclusive vehicles you get access to in the Ultimate Edition, but some of these are only available during chapter one for story reasons. The only thing from the Ultimate Edition I used regularly and still use often when I play is the Vapid off-road truck. It’s fast as heck, a great option for driving on the dirt, and can be upgraded into a beast that can hold a lot of stolen loot. There’s also a classic car scavenger hunt side mission hidden behind the paywall, but after 150 hours I’ve barely interacted with that thing.

Answering the big question of “Is the Ultimate Edition worth it?” is tricky, because it depends entirely on what you value and your taste for fashion and cosmetics. I’ve provided some samples of what’s on offer and how it fits into the larger GTA 6 world.

My opinion is that if you can afford the extra $20, a few bits of the Ultimate Edition are nice and worth the upgrade. But for the most part, if you just want to play Grand Theft Auto 6 to enjoy the open world and its story, you don’t need this upgrade. You’ll have a great time with the base game and never think to yourself, “Boy, I wish there were 30 more shirts and a few more cars in this!” GTA 6 is already big. Don’t worry about making it a bit bigger.

#3650. Nvidia release hotfix for latest graphics card driver battering SSDs with excessive writes, but it looks like reverting may still be the better option

621.35 appears not to completely atone for 621.24's sins

Late last week, reports emerged of some folks having Nvidia's latest GeForce driver, 621.24, needlessly write vast amounts of data to their PC's SSD, a bug that could affect the component's lifespan at a time when replacing SSDs certainly isn't cheap. The immediate short-term solution for affected users was to roll back to a previous driver, 621.01. Sadly it appears that might still be the best way to go despite Nvidia having released a hotfix.

The hotfix, driver version 621.35, was released on November 20th and as of writing is only available to download directly from the Nvidia website. It's designed to address one issue, this being that "excessive writes to file nvlog.nvlgstg may occur in background".

"Since we have so many changes being checked in, we usually try to align driver releases with significant game or product releases," Nvidia wrote in their announcement of the hotfix. "This process has served us pretty well over the years but it has one significant weakness. Sometimes a change that is important to many users might end up sitting and waiting until we are able to release the driver. The fixes that make it in are based in part on your feedback in the Driver Feedback threads and partly on how realistic it is for us to quickly address them. These fixes (and many more) will be incorporated into the next official driver release, at which time the hotfix driver will be taken down.

"To be sure, these Hotfix drivers are beta, optional and provided as-is. They are run through a much abbreviated QA process. The sole reason they exist is to get fixes out to you more quickly. The safest option is to wait for the next WHQL certified driver. But we know that many of you are willing to try these out."

Unfortunately, it seems that based on some testing by users on r/Nvidia, the hotfix makes the situation with excessive SSD writing less bad than it is with 621.24, but doesn't eliminate the problem entirely. According to one of these users, 621.35 stops the excessive writing from starting right after you boot up and reduces the amount that's being written when the issue's at its peak, but doesn't prevent some excessive writing creeping in if hardware is left running for extended periods or left idling overnight.

Given that, rolling back to 621.01 still appears to be the most effective way of keeping the writes at an acceptable level while waiting for Nvidia to release a new driver than can permanently do away with the problem. One would hope it won't take too long, especially given the 621.24 driver still doesn't look to have been pulled offline so no one else grabs it prior to a fix arriving.

If you want to check if you're suffering from the excessive writing you'll need to open task manager, head to the 'details' tab, right click on the column header, click 'select columns', select 'I/O write bytes' from the menu of check boxes that brings up, then look for 'NVDisplay.Container.exe'. The number next that exe is in bytes, so you'll need to do some maths to work out if it's only writing a matter of MB or chunks of GB.

#3649. Infamous GTA 6 leaker CyberLeek is back, and this time the group claims to have leaked a full development build of the game

CyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game launched, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site. This new leak appears to be making good on a threat posted back in October, where the group stated its intent to release a full, playable build of the game.

Various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB. Eurogamer has seen the site and can confirm this is what the group has claimed, however I have been unable to verify the existence of any actual files. On the site, CyberLeek claims this build is from November 2026 - meaning it is very close to (if not the actual) release build. The 'executable file appears to be missing from the build, however, meaning you cannot actually - yet - get it up and running. CyberLeek is threatening to release this file at a later date, however.

"It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads. "[Cyberleek] holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent. Now. Every file except one. The main executable is held on a countdown." CyberLeek says the executable will be released earlier than planned if its crypto token reaches a predetermined value. Many of the leaks to date have been related to a CyberLeek crypto scheme. Previously, it was estimated that the group cashed out at least £200,000.

What does all this mean? There's a very realistic chance that the game could be up and running on PC soon - undercutting Rockstar's unannounced PC release by a matter of months, if current rumours are to be believed. "This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps," the statement continues. "[CyberLeek] told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons.

"If the Xbox build cannot be made to work and support holds, [CyberLeek] will work to get a PS5 build - a fallback, most likely never required. Either way: the Xbox build is going out. No double dipping for Take-Two/Rockstar." It seems these are not empty threats.

CyberLeek has been a thorn in Rockstar's side for a while now. The group initially claimed it took this action in the name of "Gamers' Rights", supposedly fighting for consumers in relation to the controversial discontinuation of game-discs and the digital-only future being pursued by game publishers. Rockstar has previously issued statements regarding the leaker, noting that the leaks are "heartbreaking" and that "this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time". Take-Two tried to subpoena Discord for information pertaining to the leaker's identity.

#3647. Ubisoft says Assassin's Creed Jade is still alive as it merges two of its Creative Houses

Ubisoft has confirmed that while Assassin's Creed Jade - its mobile entry in the series - is still in development, its focus remains with console and PC.

Speaking during the earnings call for Ubisoft's first-half results, CFO Frédérick Duguet said mobile was "still an opportunity for the medium to longer term, with games such as AC Jade on Assassin’s Creed", according to a transcript of the call published by Investing.com.

"Looking at what we can see in terms of long-term financial return, in the mindset of having a stronger focus in terms of capital allocation and financial returns, we consider that we would rather put our resources on bigger opportunities," Duguet said. "Today, we can say that console and PC remain our core focus for our biggest franchises."

He added: "The focus is really to make sure that we come with strong growth on console and PC, and notably PC, which is a more dynamic platform than ever."

Ubisoft last confirmed its China-set mobile game was still in the works in March, when it was mentioned in the publisher’s Assassin's Creed: Into 2026 blog. Assassin's Creed now sits within Vantage Studios, Ubisoft's joint venture with Tencent, which launched last year.

Ubisoft's results also confirmed some more changes to the way the company is run, with the publisher saying its new operating model is "now fully in place". Creative Houses 3 and 5 have been combined under the leadership of Julien Bares "to leverage synergies between Live experiences across platforms".

All leadership roles across the Creative Houses are now filled, too. An external general manager has been appointed for Creative House 4 and is set to join in January 2027, though Ubisoft hasn't yet confirmed who. That follows September's appointment of 2K and Amazon Games veteran Christoph Hartmann to lead Creative House 2, home to The Division, Ghost Recon, and Splinter Cell, which was renamed Massive Entertainment at the same time.

Outside the Creative Houses, Motherbrain, the team behind Ubisoft's generative AI experiment Teammates, is now a subsidiary in its own right. It's working on "smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large-scale systemic worlds". A separate unit has also been set up to look after brands that don't belong to any of the Creative Houses.

Ubisoft says the new structure is already paying off, pointing to the commercial success of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced and renewed momentum for Rainbow Six Siege, which it says ranked among the top 10 games across Xbox and PlayStation for monthly active users over the half.

That said, the publisher nonetheless posted a net loss of €254.5 million for the first half of the year, with net bookings down 16.5 percent to €644.7 million.

The news comes just hours after Ubisoft confirmed 166 job cuts at its Montréal and Québec City studios, the latest in a year of layoffs. They're part of the "major organisational, operational and portfolio reset" that Ubisoft announced in January. That initial announcement was accompanied by the news of two studio closures - affecting its Halifax mobile and Stockholm teams - plus the cancellation of six projects, including the much-delayed Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake.

Since then, 105 jobs have been cut at Red Storm Entertainment, the Ubisoft studio behind the Ghost Recon series, and around 380 employees were reportedly laid off when the publisher's Winnipeg and Belgrade teams shut in June. In October, Ubisoft closed Trials developer RedLynx and downsized its Singapore Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced team, impacting a total of approximately 120 employees. Amid all this, Ubisoft developers have been on strike in response to the publisher's sweeping layoffs.

On the weekend, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on a new Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

#3646. Nightdive's Thief remaster will make the most "infamous" Thief Gold level a little less maddening, by "just kind of pointing the player in the right direction"

On bringing Thieves Guild up to snuff with the Haunted Cathedral and co

1999's Thief Gold is widely considered the definitive incarnation of Thief: The Dark Project, adding three levels to the Looking Glass stealth sim while tidying up some bugs, but it has one grievous failing, in the eyes of many: the notorious Thieves Guild. In this all-new sixth mission, master catburglar Garrett must infiltrate the lair of a gang of pickpockets, after they filch a vase he had his eye on. The lair in question is actually very believable, as a hideout for criminals, in that it resists exploration even with a paper map. It consists of sunken, samey, obtusely arranged rooms that are made all the more headache-inducing by objectives that require a lot of backtracking.

In much the same way that I can admire a finely wrought pair of thumbscrews, I think the Thieves Guild is a clever creation, one that arguably shines when you use every ability or tactic in Garrett's possession rather than trying to ghost it. But it very easily becomes frustrating, to the point that many grizzled housebreakers advise new players to skip the level entirely. The Thieves Guild should be less frustrating in Nightdive's forthcoming Thief: The Dark Project Remastered, thanks to a more revealing spread of environmental textures and various other, furtive adjustments. As with many mods or remasters that speak of boosting the "immersion", I do worry that something valuable is being sacrificed in the process.

In the course of a wide-ranging interview about how they're reworking this most devious of Dark Projects, Nightdive producer Daniel Grayshon explained that the map changes are "more in terms of background tech", than altering the fundamental design or introducing details that oblige different strategies. "They've gone into these levels in a sensible way to fix some practical problems with them, like some issues where you might be able to climb up to a place that you shouldn't have been able to climb up before," he commented.

The Thief remaster team have taken more liberties, seemingly, with some of the Thief Gold maps. "Because some of the levels that were introduced in Thief Gold - they felt quite blocky and quite rushed, maybe, as you go through them," Grayshon explained. "But our team again, they've been able to go through and completely renovate some of these levels. The Opera House now feels in some parts like an actual Opera House, instead of a couple of blocky rooms. So I think players will really look at these and think, oh yeah, these kinds of details make sense, without it being too disruptive or too immersion breaking…"

"One particular - maybe people will consider infamous - level of the Gold package would be the Thieves Guild," Grayshon added. "The Thieves Guild is, if I were to sum it up kind of briefly, it is maybe two hours of walking through what feels like sewers, the same environment over and over again. There was no real visual distinction as to where you are in the level.

"So, we acknowledged pretty quickly that we need to go in and look at the Thieves Guild and fix it up, and what we've been able to do is texture it a lot more effectively. Give areas distinct looks, without compromising any of the gameplay again, like I mentioned. So we've put a bit more signposting around as well. Nothing that's going to be intrusive or immersion breaking again. Just kind of pointing the player in the right direction, as well as some other little things that I'm not going to spoil too much, but I think players will maybe appreciate the effort that we've done for this one."

In general, Nightdive's broad aim has been "bringing those Gold levels up to the quality of the original and then taking all of those levels and then bumping them up to the next level - almost Thief 2 levels of quality in its environment design, especially in some of the mansions, and some of the later levels," Grayshon said. "That's the level we were aiming for."

I have Several Thoughts about Grayshon's thoughts above (yes, people who dislike huffy armchair theory, this is your cue to skip to the comments). One is that I continue to dislike "immersion" as an ideal, though I recognise that many devs just use it as easy shorthand for a bunch of ways of doing art, sound and interface design. I think it often translates to uninvestigated enthusiasm for photorealistic fidelity and experiences that feel "smooth" and "engaging" enough to induce a kind of chemical trance. Many of the games I consider most valuable are cranky and unwilling and jarring, requiring you to think critically about the simulation rather than 'losing yourself' inside it. As regards the original Thief specifically, I enjoy how its nigh-magical stealth induces feelings of wavering dissociation, and keeps me guessing about the solidity of my own body.

Secondly, there's the age-old argument that if you're going to preserve a game faithfully, you should preserve what it did badly. The Thieves Guild is a legend among players, much as Blighttown is among Dark Souls players and the Library is among fans of Halo: Combat Evolved. You learn much about the methodology of Thief at large from the guild's stifling contours, and it's thrilling to witness a bunch of very smart designers take a swing at a concept and not quite connect. I'll try to hold onto that rousing sentiment, when I'm playing the remaster and struggling to remember where they hid that damn vase.

Welcome to a brand new week of GTA 6 still blowing everyone's minds. We will probably be covering this beat for months if not years as players and game developers continue unearthing new discoveries and technical marvels, with one prominent dev comparing GTA 6 to the Great Pyramids in Egypt.

Mark Richard Davies, game director at Naughty Dog and game designer on The Last of Us 2, is the latest game developer to appear awe-stricken in reaction to Rockstar's opus. A colleague of Davies, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet world design director Michael Barclay, recently said GTA 6 appears to him "as a Bugatti Veyron would to a nervous Victorian child," underscoring the unprecedented depth and scale of the game.

In a new tweet, Davies says we might never find every piece of the GTA 6 puzzle and jokingly predicts we'll one day discover extraterrestrial intelligence hiding in its DNA. "GTA VI is the Great Pyramids of Game Development," he says. "As in, people will be asking for centuries how it was possible and we will eventually conclude that aliens made it."

GTA VI is the Great Pyramids of Game Development. As in, people will be asking for centuries how it was possible and we will eventually conclude that aliens made it.November 22, 2026

In response to a commenter who rightfully points out Rockstar's "8 to 13" year development cycle and estimated $1 billion budget, Davis simply says, "I'm sure the pyramids were expensive too," seemingly acknowledging that one part of Rockstar's magic is unfathomable financial resources. For instance, the thing that amazes Davies the most about GTA 6, in his words, is "Every NPC having voice lines and reactions. The sheer size of the script must be mind boggling." The level of interactivity and variety in GTA 6's NPCs is hugely immersive, but that wouldn't have been possible if Rockstar and parent company Take-Two Interactive didn't have the money to pay that amount of voice and performance capture artists.

All that said, in addition to lots and lots of money, there's an element to Rockstar's sterling track record for genre-defining releases that has very little to do with money and a lot to do with extremely talented individuals firing on all cylinders and a unified vision from legacy leadership. But, you know, having $1 billion dollars to spend certainly doesn't hurt.

#3644. Here Are Some Super Useful Control Shortcuts GTA 6 Doesn’t Tell You About

I’ve played over 150 hours of Grand Theft Auto 6. You might think I’ve seen it all, and that I know everything there is to know about the game. Nope! I’m still discovering new mechanics, features, and open-world moments after all this time. This includes some very handy control shortcuts I recently learned about that will make your life in Vice City a little easier.

First off, let’s start with the whole reason I wanted to write this blog. Did you know that you can quickly toggle your car radio on and off without having to enter a submenu? All you have to do is double-tap left on the D-pad, and Jason or Lucia will turn the radio on or off.

I had no idea you could do this until I saw people sharing it on Reddit. The game doesn’t explain this shortcut, as far as I can tell. I couldn’t even find it mentioned in the in-game help menu, which does include lots of other nifty tips and tricks.

Here’s another trick I just learned about: You can double-tap the circle/B button while in a car to cycle the headlights between off, high beams, and low beams.

I thought you had to hold left on the D-pad to open up the vehicle submenu to turn off the headlights, but nope! And again, this isn’t mentioned in the help menu and if a prompt appeared during the normal course of the game to explain this, I and many others must have missed it.

Here’s another useful thing you can do inside cars: If you double-tap the triangle/Y button while driving, you’ll exit the vehicle without turning off the engine or radio.

GTA 6‘s help menu does call this out and mentions you can do this at speed to have your car drive into something while you roll out the side to safely. But again, I can’t remember a single time when the game forced me to do this or taught me that it was possible. I learned from a random post online. I guess I should have dug through the help menu more, but come on, who is doing that in Grand Theft Auto?

Another feature mentioned in the help menu that I just learned about is the ability to click the right stick in and yell at nearby drivers. Rockstar refers to this as the road rage button, and it’s a good thing to have in a game where NPC drivers, inspired by real Floridian drivers, suck shit and drive like maniacs.

One more useful control trick: You can double-tap the triangle/Y button while driving a boat to get up and walk around the deck while the boat keeps on cruising.

The next time I boot up GTA 6, I’m going to start double-tapping random buttons during different parts of the game to see what other hidden shortcuts and control options Rockstar has buried in this massive game. And if you want some more useful hidden features, check out this blog about how to flip cars and sit anywhere you want in GTA 6.Â

Lots of people will tell you that Grand Theft Auto 6's Lucia Caminos marks the series' first female protagonist. Lots of people are, of course, wrong. GTA 1 had eight selectable protagonists, four of whom were women, while GTA 2 for the Game Boy Color let you play protags Candy or Gretchen (along with a bunch of other men) in addition to the PlayStation game's default Claude Speed.

That vital pedantry out of the way, it's undeniable that Lucia is GTA's first female protagonist since the series became the culture-swallowing goliath it is today. In a chat with CBC's As It Happens, GTA OG Brian Baglow said he reckons it's "long, long overdue".

Baglow, credited as a writer on the original GTA and who served as "head of propaganda and indoctrination" at DMA Design (the studio that would become Rockstar North) in the '90s, said that back in the day of GTA 1, the devs didn't even have a script. "We started with a tech demo, a way of moving around a city… I came in to actually add the story, add the script, after the levels had been built".

That was mostly a process of, shall we say, finding inspiration: "we were making it up as we went along… it was a case of going into every crime movie, every heist, every caper, every TV show, cop show, crime drama, and lifting elements that I hoped would resonate with people".

Baglow sounds, rightfully, rather proud of his time spent working on such an important series, but he has his qualms as he casts his eye back over it. "The representation of women, it has not been good, and that's putting it very mildly", he says, "so I'm delighted that we now have not only a female protagonist, but a Hispanic female protagonist. I think it's been long, long overdue, and I can't wait to get to grips with the game and see how in-depth it goes.

"I think it's showing a level of maturation because from the very earliest days it was a very young group of almost entirely male developers in Scotland".

#3642. Blizzard wants to "get rid" of best-in-slot items in World of Warcraft: Forever by introducing situationally strong gear

"BIS is not a good thing for a game that's supposed to be about role-playing."

With World of Warcraft: Forever's first raids set to release in early December, developers of the game have spoken about endgame itemisation and their desire to disrupt the "best-in-slot" (BIS) mindset that's been at the core of WoW's progression for years.

This information stems from the latest episode of the official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast. In it, senior game designer Aidan Moon revealed his philosophy around the game's itemisation, which he played - and plays - a major role in designing.

"I essentially want to get rid of BIS," Moon said. "I think BIS is not a good thing for a video game that's supposed to be about role-playing. That's why I've introduced the creature subtype system, where things are more effective against murlocs [for example]. We've introduced the biome system too, and in the raid it's different."

He gave an example from upcoming raid Barrow Deeps, which will be split into different biomes that offer opportunities for such creature subtype gear to be put to use. "If you go to the left wing that's snowy; if you go to the right wing, that's haunted; if you go down below, that's cavernous. ... I think your BIS should be different for every single boss if you're making a theoretical BIS list."

Moon acknowledged that the system is open for players to interact with to the extent they're comfortable with. Some players might bring optimised gear for certain bosses, while others might not, opting instead for generally good gear to perform well regardless of the fight.

It's an excitingly different approach that goes against the established norms of WoW's endgame raiding. In other versions in World of Warcraft, gear progression is more linear: people go into raids with an idea of what gear drops are best for their character, and intentionally hunt these pieces to replace the set they're wearing. It's a vertical sense of progression. Will theoretically having multiple sets of equipment, for multiple situations, change this?

Best-in-slot gear is an especially pertinent topic in WoW Forever at the moment, given the most dedicated players are reaching max level, or nearing it, and are hunting for items in preparation for the upcoming raid. I'm currently ticking off equipment from a best-in-slot list for a Balance Druid. Whether this player behavior will change when the changes are implemented remains to be seen. Perhaps the approach will expand, with players continuing to hunt down generally accepted 'good' items while also seeking side pieces that provide situational bonuses along the way.

The Blizzard discussion on raid itemisation went beyond standard power items. Chase items, those with especially low drop rates, were also talked about by Moon, noting that Barrow Deeps continues several such items that he hopes will keep players returning to it for years to come.

The items Moon is likely referring to here probably relate to mounts, pets, situational gear, and perhaps campfire bonuses.

For example, I obtained an upgraded campfire earlier in the game that allows a greater campfire to be built that allows more buff items to be placed around it.This has essentially locked me in as a campfire slave for the upcoming raid tier, and valuable to a raid composition.

World of Warcraft: Forever has proven extremely popular since its early November release. The game broke franchise records for Blizzard on launch, and has more weekly players than WoW has seen in 15 years. Judging from early impressions of World of Warcraft: Forever, the game has real merit.

#3641. Nvidia reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO following alleged affairs, as US government support renders 'please give me my job back, go USA' a highly persuasive plea

Sexy leather jacket man's successor is exact same sexy leather jacket man, it turns out

Yep, he's back. Less than two weeks after Jensen Huang resigned from being CEO of Nvidia following reports of multiple affairs, the company's board have reinstated him "effective immediately".

"The board of directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr Huang, after which the board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candour and ability to lead Nvidia," the company announced. "In the process of reaching its decision, the board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk."

"The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," added recently appointed chairman Harvey Jones, who'll remain in the post following Huang's return. Colette Kress, who served as interim CEO during Huang's short break, will go back to just being chief financial officer.

"I am honoured to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang declared. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment."

Oh, and Nvidia's board added that the independent investigation they set in motion "in light of recent reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort" will "proceed to conclusion". Huang "fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it", they noted.

Since resigning amid the scandal, Huang had made it clear he'd be open to returning to his post if the Nvidia board okayed it and had several powerful people either call for his reinstatement or declare they'd consider hiring him. "The country needs Jensen’s leadership at Nvidia in order to ensure the success and prosperity of not only the company, but the American economy," one such advocate, US president Donald Trump, has reportedly posted to cursed hellcape Truth social. Huang is a "great patriot and national treasure", the Trumpeter added.

So, there you go. I'm not saying that you're totally immune to consequences for alleged actions that'd lose any normal person their job for far more than 11 days if you're mates with the American president, but it sure does look like that, doesn't it? Hope Nvidia didn't throw out any leather jackets Huang couldn't manage to carry out of the building with him.

#3640. These Are The 11 Best Romances BioWare Ever Made

BioWareDragon AgeKnights of the Old RepublicMass EffectRoman

When it comes to digital romances, BioWare was one of the best to ever do it. Though the studio wasnât the first to implement romanceable companions, BioWare set the example for what a fulfilling digital romance could be. Its work made the right people mad, with Mass Effectâs same-sex relationships generating sensational segments on national TV networks way back in 2007.Â

BioWareâs dedication to inclusion resulted in some of the best AAA examples of queer love, kink dynamics, and gender expression in relationships, as well as how trauma informs romance and sex, and even senior love. At other times, BioWare romances were just fun little one-offs with no strings attached because relationships are like that sometimes in real life, too. They gave us some of the funniest lines in video game romance and some of the most heartbreaking, and all of them truly memorable.

With BioWare now gone, other studios have stepped in to carry the love-torch, but like your first kiss, you never forget your first BioWare romance. Here are the studioâs best.

By any objective estimation, Garrus Vakarian should not be appealing to women. He is a 6-foot-plus armored bird lizard with a mouth that reminds people of a certain age of the movie Tremors, but he remains universally at the top of any Mass Effect enjoyerâs âhear me outâ list. Not only is he a male whose voice is pure sex; heâs also the sweetest, funniest, most capable sidekick a girl could ask for.Â

Whatâs uniquely great about his romance is that instead of having both him and (female) Shepard declare their interest and have that be that, the game makes space for the considerable logistics that might be involved in interspecies intercourse. Some of the Mass Effect seriesâ funniest moments revolve around Shepard and Garrus trying to figure out how to make this crazy thing called love work.Â  â Ash Parrish

Â TaliâZorah vas Normandy is the romance option for folks who enjoy the âfalling in love with your best friendâs little sisterâ trope. Even though Tali is not technically anyoneâs little sister, thatâs the vibe she brings to the Normandy along with a sharp wit and a very low alcohol tolerance.Â

Like with the Garrus relationship for female Shepards, the Tali romance is pre-occupied with getting around the logistics of hooking up with a being for whom the tiniest bit of open-air exposure beyond her self-contained biosuit can have life-threatening implications. Like Liara, Tali transforms from a tech geek to a badass, but never quite loses her awkward and shy nature. Her romance in Mass Effect 3 is possibly the gameâs best because Commander Shepard gets to be the ultimate boyfriend, gifting his girlfriend, whose people have been living as nomads across the galaxy for centuries, her very own planet to settle down on. â Ash Parrish

Liara is the Mass Effect love interest who writes Commander Shepardâs name in the stars. Over the course of three games, Liara romancers get the treat of seeing her grow from a naive, adorable nerd into a formidable badass at the head of her own slightly criminal empire. Being an Asari, a race of blue alien women who have the ability to reproduce with literally any species, Liara can romance either Shepard.Â

Itâs her romance that made BioWare the subject of salacious segments on Fox News declaring Mass Effect little better than pornography and questioning the âappropriatenessâ of depicting same-sex relationships in a video game âfor kidsâ. Sheâs the one you can plan a family with as Shepard and Liara talk about a future filled with little blue children, offering hope that some part of Shepardâs story continues after the events of Mass Effect 3. – Ash Parrish

Solas gets put in the BioWare romance hall of fame for being one of the best toxic boyfriends in all of video games. He is good specifically for how bad he hurts you, emotionally and physically. Solas shows up in Dragon Age Inquisition as an elven apostate mageâessentially a magical hobo. A female elven Inquisitor takes him in like a lost puppy and eventually a romance begins to bloom.Â

He shares secrets pertaining to elven history, and talks of big plans to save their people from the oppression of humans. But during the moment when most other BioWare romances would be reaching their climax, he breaks up with you and wonât tell you why. Itâs eventually revealed that heâs the one responsible for setting the events of Inquisition in motion, resulting in the world tearing itself apart and in the Inquisitor having a magic hand thatâs slowly tearing her apart. That betrayal inspired an entire fandom of Dragon Age players who either wanted to redeem him when he returned as the big bad in Veilguard or, like I and many others wanted, to kill him. â Ash Parrish

Emmrich was not on my radar as a love interest in Dragon Age: The Veilguard. Heâs old! And not like âelf whoâs lived for thousands of yearsâ old, heâs regular degular, graying-at-the-temples, wrinkles-in-the-face old. Once again, BioWare surprises and delights with a romance designed to represent the fact that love can be found at any time in life and sexual desire doesnât disappear after a certain age.Â

Emmrichâs romance doesnât shy away from the reality that Rook is younger than he is and heâll likely pass away (or not, depending on choices you can make) before they do. His romance asks players to consider that very real part of life in a way that just doesnât get depicted in video games. AND!!! The fact that Emmrich is an old man doesnât mean the sex is dry and boring. I was delightedâdelighted I tell you!âwhen in the postcoital afterglow he was up, walking around and asking my Rook if she wanted some food while I was still half in bed. Old man broke MY back. Respect. â Ash Parrish

Alistair is the number one BioWare cutie patootie. In Dragon Age: Origins heâs just a good wholesome farm boy conscripted into drinking demon blood that will eventually kill him. Alistair was my very first BioWare romance and I instantly fell for his golden-retriever charm. The Iron Bull is to Dragon Age romances what Garrus and Tali are to Mass Effect romances in that I canât believeâbut am delightedâthat BioWare went for it and made the most ânon-humanâ character in your squad actually romanceable. Morrigan from Dragon Age: Origins, with her dark makeup and impossible outfit literally held together with string, seems like an âI can fix herâ romance when actually sheâs a âShe can make me worseâ girl. A male Grey Warden can conceive a child with her, one you see grow throughout the Dragon Age quadrilogy, but except for a few brief moments throughout the series, the Grey Warden never really gets the chance to settle down with his family, making her romance part love story, part tragedy. â Ash Parrish

Kaidan is the first male love interest in the Mass Effect series, but in truth, his romantic relationship is best when viewed as a slow burn across the entire trilogy. Thatâs why a romantic relationship with him as Male Shepard, which was only made an option in Mass Effect 3 when BioWare decided to finally implement same-sex relationships for men, is one of the most profound love stories in the series. It suggests Kaidan and Shepard have been pining for each other for years, only to finally confess their feelings as the entire world is ending around them. Every kiss stolen between missions and military meetings is making up for years of âwill-they-wonât-theysâ and all that time they spent not even speaking to each other during Mass Effect 2. Now, theyâre finally considering a future with one another that they donât even know if theyâll get to have. The galaxy rests on their shoulders, but their sights are set on something smaller: the chance to spend just one more second of time together after all the time they foolishly wasted getting to this point. This all culminates in the twoâs first and only on-screen âI love youâ as Shepard makes a dash for the Citadel at the end of Mass Effect 3, hoping that whatever he finds there might guarantee that future, or, if it canât, at least create one that Kaidan is alive to see. â Kenneth Shepard

As a Mass Effect diehard, I have a soft spot for KOTORâs Carth because heâs voiced by Kaidan actor Raphael Sbarge, but I will also give his romance, in which he reckons with the loss of one life and tries to imagine another, its flowers as one of BioWareâs early examples of a relationship tinged with grief and loss. He had a family once, and he lost them in an orbital strike by the Republic; his desire for revenge consumed him. Like many good revenge stories, KOTOR sees its would-be avenger reckon with what comes after the deed has been done, and if youâre pursuing a relationship with him, it might be you. BioWare games have you meet people at various stages of their lives, and thereâs something poignant about knowing that you might not have been your partnerâs first love, and that theyâve lived lives full of both triumph and tragedy. Carth canât change the past, but youâre there to help him envision something new waiting for him on the other side of this struggle. â Kenneth Shepard

The Fenris romance is like a recipe that calls for you to add a little bit of spice, but you accidentally pour the entire bottle of hot sauce into the concoction and then realize thatâs exactly what it needed. Fenris is an angry person, having been forced into slavery under the Tevinter magisters and conditioned to view magic with skepticism at best, disdain at worst. So, what if he fell in love with a mage that he could not have been more ideologically opposed to? The Rivalry Romance, in which Dragon Age II protagonist Hawke repeatedly calls him out on his absolute hatred of magic users,hits with the kind of intensity your favorite AO3 fanfic can only dream of. Itâs hot, heavy, heart-wrenching and, if you commit to doing the work to trust one another, has a happy ending.Â  Well, as happy as Dragon Age II can muster, I suppose. Trust in the face of a lifetime of conditioning is hard to come by, and allowing yourself to be vulnerable to something youâve been taught doesnât see you as a person feels downright impossible. Yet Fenris and Hawke find a way. â Kenneth Shepard

Despite the fantastical framing, Dorianâs love story in Dragon Age: Inquisition is one that too many queer people are familiar with. He comes from an unsupportive family, having fled his home in Tevinter after his sexuality interfered with their planned legacy. A new trailer for Avengers: Doomsday is here, and fans are pretty convinced that Steve Rogers is actually Loki.

In the new trailer we see a whole lot of Steve Rogers and Peggy Carter back at their home (though we have no idea what time period or universe they live in)... but the Steve we see outside in the real world walking alongside Thor seems a bit different.

"That was a good speech back there," Steve says in the clip. Thor replies, "Yours felt a little average by Cap's standards, don't you think?" Steve then smiles, holds up Mjölnir, and says, "This doesn't bother you, does it?" It would most definitely bother Thor if Loki got to use Mjölnir as a weapon, seeing as only the pure of heart (like Steve Rogers) can hold that hammer, and Loki is far from it.

This still doesn't explain how Loki is able to leave his post at the center of the universe holding up Yggdrasil... but I'm sure that'll be explained.

#3635. Finally, some former Valorant and Sky devs have answered the call for a Peak-style platformer about throwing a cat through a hole in spacetime

It's embarrassing that we had to wait this long

As a mature and sophisticated artform, videogames offer answers to many of life's important questions, such as "how many spaceships is too many spaceships?" (a trick question, obviously) or "which 12th century BC civilisation was better at playing Age of Empires 2?" Lately, I have been wrestling with the enigma of how I should transport a sleeping cat in a snowglobe up a psychedelic mountain. According to Whisk, I should phone a friend.

In this first-person co-op platformer - created in Unreal Engine, with both online multiplayer and splitscreen support - you and a mate play Luna and Foam, two rock-hopping magic children with nothing better to do than lob hermetically sealed felines through tears in reality itself. Egad! Apparently the cats are fine with this. You'll have to work together to traverse astral watercolour landscapes, hurling and catching the kitty while trying not to tumble into the abyss.

You can also catch each other's arms and haul each other onto safe ground, which puts this in approximately the same bracket as the well-liked Peak. Other Neat Tricks include bouncing the starry-eyed moggies from soap bubbles, swinging from strands of green snot (?), and springboarding from tornadoes.

The cats remain blissfully unconscious throughout, smiling in their slumber right up to the point when you crack their crystal prisons. If you're familiar with cats, the penalty for breaking their domes may seem rather mild. I was hoping for something along the lines of Peter Puppy having a rage-out in Earthworm Jim.

Would it surprise you to learn that one or more of the people working on Whisk is a former developer of Sky: Children of Light, the open world swoop 'em up from thatgamecompany? I imagine you might not consider that startling – the two games both look a little like the result of somebody inhaling burnt banana skins. But you might be giddier to hear that one or more of the Whisk devs is also a veteran of Riot's Counter-Strike descendant Valorant. I'm pretty sure Valorant doesn't have any cat-throwing, but I'm prepared to be proven wrong.

It's coming to Steam early access early in 2027, and there's a demo on Steam right now with eight levels and 10 cats to "rescue". People are already bragging in the forums about their leaderboard placements – monsters!

#3634. GTA 6 day-one sales are enormous, estimates suggest, making previous $2 billion opening weekend predictions seem conservative

Grand Theft Auto 6 is estimated to have sold nearly 25 million copies in one day, generating approximately $2.5bn in sales revenue - a staggering result that's beyond even what even observers were predicting.

The estimates come from data-tracking company Sensor Tower (spotted by VGC), which has been watching GTA 6 pre-orders closely for weeks, updating estimates daily based on (unspecified) data that it collects.

Should the results be accurate, it'll dramatically eclipse GTA 6's $1bn in three days result. It'll also put GTA 6 on track to reach the eye-watering $3.25bn to $5.2bn week-one sales estimates for GTA 6.

So far, Rockstar has said nothing in relation to GTA 6's sales since the game was released around the world yesterday. Parent company Take-Two has said the game's pre-orders were tracking "well above expectations, and GTA 6 broke pre-order records on both the PlayStation Store and the Xbox Store, though, so all signs point to a record-breaking release. The question is "by how much?".

Reaction to GTA 6 has been glittering. Chris awarded GTA 6 five golden stars in Eurogamer's review, calling it "a game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale". "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that."

"As long as you have great game feel and a great game loop, I think you're going to be OK"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The burgeoning AI takeover that ramped up a few years back has caused a lot of human stress for a lot of different reasons. Workers across many industries fear for their livelihoods, and on a much more existential scale, there's been substantial debate from industry leaders about whether AI will one day turn hostile and bring about the extinction of the human species, but that's a topic for another publication. For people who make video games, the frightening advancement of AI capabilities means it's easier for nefarious wannabe game developers to take a legitimate game, toss it into an AI prompt, and come out the other side with a legally distinct copycat.

One way to curb the potential of your game being cloned with AI tools to shorten the time between the game's announcement and release, reckons Alex Nichiporchik, CEO of tinyBuild, the publisher behind the ironically named cyberpunk shopkeeper sim, Probably Stolen. Nichiporchik tells GamesIndustry.biz he thinks "the biggest talking point over the next half year is going to be the time to market, and how devs are now afraid of how AI copies their games."

Much more important than market timing, in Nichiporchik's view, is what he calls "game feel." I probably don't need to explain this, but game feel generally refers to how a game feels to play, who woulda thunk? In other words, it's the tactile sensation of controlling a game on a moment-to-moment level, and it's something generative AI has been shown time and time again to get hideously wrong. Nichiporchik goes a step further and says AI is literally incapable of nailing game feel, and that game developers shouldn't worry about AI clones for that reason.

"Devs should just think about 'How do you make [your game] more difficult to copy?' Because game feel is impossible to copy," he says. "You can have all the references and you can have a lot of outsourcing companies trying to copy your game with proper designers, and they still fail. Why? Because of the game feel.

"As long as you have great game feel and a great game loop, I think you're going to be OK. And the other theory that keeps on confirming itself is time, right? The more time people spend in your game, the more sales you're going to get. So look at your time spent and create great game feel that people love, and everything else is secondary, I think."

Probably Stolen was announced on August 3 and released on October 28, an unusually brief window between reveal and launch, and Nichiporchik says it's already shifted more than a million units. It seems tinyBuild and developer Questing Goose Studio's success has been undeterred by AI clones unable to flood the market in time, or maybe it's the title's unclonable game feel.

#3632. Red Dead Redemption Movie And TV Rights Could Reportedly Cost $100 Million

Grand Theft Auto VIGTA 6MoviesRed Dead Redemption 2Rockstar Games

With many legacy franchises in decline and few new ones taking off, Hollywood has turned to video games for big box office blockbusters. There have been huge success stories like Minecraft and big bombs like Borderlands. But some of the biggest video game series have yet to make the jump to the silvers screen. Chief among them is Grand Theft Auto. Could that be about to change?

According to a report in The Ankler this week, the answer is no. Multiple sources told the outlet that Rockstar Games isn’t interested in doing a movie adaptation of GTA. It makes sense, in a way, since GTA has increasingly become a series about bringing prestige, cinematic storytelling to the messy, systems-driven gameplay of open-world gaming. Putting that engine in reverse would be a bit like turning the video game version of Indiana Jones back into a movie. Who would ever do that?

But it sounds like Rockstar, owned by Take-Two, is interested in shopping around the rights for a movie or TV adaptation of its Western open-world series, Red Dead Redemption. The Ankler adds that a number of $100 million was at one point thrown around for the price of licensing Red Dead. It points out that Amazon paid $250 million for the TV rights to Lord of the Rings.

Red Dead is in a similar lane to The Last of Us, which HBO managed to thread the needle on making into a prestige television show that still hooked fans of the game. It’s easy to imagine a similarly placed streamer doing the same for Rockstar’s IP, with internal executives pointing to mood boards that include the critical success of things like Deadwood and the commercial appeal of things like Yellowstone.

âWeâre very careful about line extensions because this is a creative company and our goal is to make the best entertainment on earth. Entertainment weâre always proud of,â Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, who used to be COO at 20th Century Fox, said in an interview on The David Rubenstein Show November 12. âWe would make a movie or television show based on our intellectual property if our creative teams were passionate about it. If they thought that would somehow engage and delight our consumers. Itâs a high bar to do that. And of course, thereâs always a risk of failure. So we donât rule it out, but weâre very, very selective.â

He’d given shareholders a more detailed account of this reasoning back in 2023 during Hollywood’s Barbenheimer-craze”

The hit ratios in the motion picture business are vastly lower than they are in the interactive entertainment business. Our hit ratios for console properties are in the 80 percent or 90 percent. The hit ratio for a well-run movie studio is around 30 percent, which is to say there’s a 70 percent chance that the movie that we license could fail. And so in success, the number, in terms of the benefit to our bottom line…it’s not zero, but it’s not really material to what we do around here. And in failure, we run the risk of compromising the underlying intellectual property.

The race to adapt other popular game franchises is already well underway. According to The Ankler, Amazon, Netflix, and FX are paying between $15 million and $25 million per episode for adaptations of Tomb Raider, Assassin’s Creed, and Far Cry. Those are essentially mid-range Hollywood blockbuster budgets.

But Take-Two hasn’t rushed to turn its IP into streaming adaptations, and following the disaster that was the Borderlands movie, which was in production prior to it acquiring series maker Gearbox Entertainment, it has good reason to be. It’s games are already breaking sales and revenue records that Hollywood can’t compete with (GTA 6‘s day-one revenue eclipsed Avengers: Endgame). Why jeopardize that for a small side deal? A good Red Dead show could help the game sell ten million more copies, but a bad one could severely hamper its growing popularity beyond traditional gaming audiences.

“They thought weâd be blinded by the lights and that just wasn’t the case,” Rockstar cofounder Dan Houser, who left to form his own entertainment company, said last year when talking about past discussions. “We had what we considered to be multi billion dollar IP, and the economics never made sense. The risk never made sense. In those days, the perception was that games made poor-quality movies.”

A 2008 adaptation of Max Payne, which Remedy Entertainment developed but Rockstar publishes, starred Mark Wahlberg and was moderately successful at the box office but critically panned with a 15 percent on Rotten Tomatoes. The misstep didn’t doom the series, which eventually got Max Payne 3 and is currently slated for remakes of the first two games, but it’s clearly not the sort of thing Rockstar or Take-Two are interested in repeating, especially when legacy movie studios are in the decline and they’re the entertainment industry’s new big shots.

#3631. "Don't let this happen again": GTA 6 hacker who pleaded guilty to 2022 Rockstar Games breach released under supervision

Case "highlights the dangers that young people can end up being drawn to online", according to City of London Police

A hacker who pleaded guilty to the 2022 hacking breach of Rockstar Games, which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net, has been released under supervision. The hacker, Arion Kurtaj, has also a five year long serious crime prevention order which will restrict what he can do online.

The BBC report that Kurtaj has been released on licence after serving most of a seven-year sentence. On licence means his release is subject to a number of conditions. According to the UK Government website, the exact nature of these conditions varies from person to person and case to case, as they've got be "considered necessary and proportionate". However, things like needing not to commit any more crimes, not travel abroad, and live under the supervision of community offender manager are cited as part of a set of "standard licence conditions" outlined by the government site.

Kurtaj has also been given a serious crime prevention order to run for five years, restricting his activity online. It includes bans from using both Telegram and Discord.

According to the BBC, the judge told Kurtaj Yyou are a very talented young man," and warned him: "Don't let this happen again." City of London Police said the case "highlights the dangers that young people can end up being drawn to online".

Kurtaj pleaded guilty on November 16th at Woolwich Crown Court to the 2022 Rockstar Games hack, as well as a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17. Now aged 21, he was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital indefinitely, due to the severity of his autism, but was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial.

90 clips of unfinished GTA 6 were flung online by the 2022 hack, with Rockstar having refused to cooperate with Kurtaj's demand via an internal Slack channel that the company contact him on massaging app Telegram within 24 hours. Rockstar claimed the breach cost them $5m million to recover from, in addition to staff having to waste thousands of hours.

Earlier this year, GTA 6 suffered yet another leak, with a hacker or hackers going by 'Cyberleek' posting various videos of the game in action. Rockstar and parent company Take-Two quickly sprung into action, taking down videos, filing subpoenas, and issuing a statement that called the leak "heartbreaking".

Cyberleek has since claimed to have lobbed a near-complete Xbox build of GTA 6 onto the net, while withholding a main executable file they threatened to release subsequently. Online sources claim the executable has now also been leaked, though this has not been independently verified.

"Did they make us make Dragon Age 2? No. But they made us do something."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

"Someone, I won't name them just so I don't get them in trouble, once said that EA doesn't shoot you, it puts a gun on the table and then comes in everyday and asks you if you'll shoot yourself, and they just keep coming in over and over until eventually you just are like 'Ugh, fine. Just stop bugging me about it, I'll do it.' And so the reality is that EA can legitimately say 'we didn't make BioWare do this, they chose to do this', but if you dig underneath that statement the reality is that the options on the table were all terrible. We chose the least terrible of the options." Via an interview with Pembridge.

Last month we got the devastating news that BioWare, the legendary studio that brought us Mass Effect, Dragon Age, and classics like Neverwinter Nights, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, and the OG Baldur's Gate was being shut down. The decision was made by EA, just a year after it was acquired by a consortium made up of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and investment firms Silver Lake and Affinity Partners (owned by the son-in-law of US president Donald Trump, Jared Kushner).

The reasons? Underperforming games. Dragon Age: The Veilguard didn't hit the mark, Andromeda wasn't well received, and Anthem, the live-service shooter, shut its servers down for good earlier this year.

It's a bad string of events for sure, but former Dragon Age boss Mark Darrah doesn't believe that it's all down to BioWare's poor management. The studio was backed into a corner by EA and the pressure to perform.

Decisions like using the Frostbite Engine, "making Dragon Age 2", and "shipping Anthem" were all products of BioWare needing to hit financial targets set out by EA. "They basically said 'Gotta hit your financials, so what are you going to do?' Darrah says. "'Are you going to ship KOTOR a year sooner than you think is going to happen? No. Are you going to pull Mass Effect in a year? No. It was never clear what the consequence of 'no' was, and it still isn't. But it seemed really dire at the time. So you gotta do something, so what are you going to do? Did they make us make Dragon Age 2? No. But they made us do something."

#3629. Total War: Warhammer 40,000 breaks the game into star system mini-campaigns, each with their own stories and objectives

"We want to represent the scale of the whole galaxy."

There is perhaps nothing so brutal in a Total War game than getting an army full of elite units wiped out, and it appears that pain remains a factor in the upcoming Total War conversion of : Warhammer 40,000. Creative Assembly also has some nifty ideas around breaking the game into mini-campaigns for each star system you visit.

In an hour-long deep-dive livestream of Total War: Warhammer 40,000, developer Creative Assembly demonstrated the game in action, focusing initially on how armies navigate from planet to planet. Each star system apparently acts as a "contained campaign" you can hop between in the game.

The star system the stream focused on is Praevoss, a mid-sized collection of planets: three of which you can land on and fight on, while the others are smaller and unable to support your tactical warfare shenanigans. Once you're finished with a star system, you move on, carrying over units and unlocked skills.

"First and foremost, we want to represent the scale of the whole galaxy, which is just not possible on a single Total War map," Creative Assembly explained on the livestream. "You'd never be able to engage with it. Part of the point is to break this up a bit and allow us to have some more interesting and more bespoke narratives going on. So each of these star systems has a premise, has a narrative, has a specific setup, a specific start, [and] specific victory objectives that you've got to go and do."

One of the objectives highlighted in the livestream was an Ork Scourge, which required the player - controlling Space Marines - to hold the planet while eradicating the Ork presence.

As you can imagine, much of the stream was dedicated to the fleet of spaceships at your disposal - fleet movement and management, and the abilities they provide to your armies such as orbital bombardments. There was also detail on how ships transport troops, as well as the upgrades you can build to further enhance their power.

On the topic of transporting troops, the developers focused on the small number of expensive but powerful Space Marines they controlled. These Space Marine armies come with a potentially "devastating" cost if you mess up and lose your armies during one of the star system campaigns.

"Losing a whole army of Space Marines is pretty devastating," the developers explained. "That's intentional, as that's a whole Space Marine chapter. Like, losing an army of Space Marines, that's a massive deal for them. It would take them decades to recover from that."

Total War: Warhammer 40,000 is set to release some time in 2027, though no specific date has been established as of writing. Much has been seen at this point on its gameplay, galactic or otherwise. As we near the end of the year, fans are clamouring for official word on when they can take to the stars.

#3628. Might and Magic meets, er, paper in sunny new RPG Rise of Furax, a turn-based island tale that is entirely drawn by hand

Is that you, Mr Sneeze? What have they done to you, boy?

Literal decades ago, I tried to make a first-person RPG in HyperCard. I got as far as a fateful town gate confrontation before hitting the cap on slides for the shareware version. I mention this because new, 100% "hand-drawn" first-person dungeon crawler Rise of Furax is uncannily redolent of my long-lost HyperCard game.

This risks being a) a terrible indictment of the game's visual direction, and b) an insinuation that developers Rap2h are dastardly rip-off artists, so let me elaborate that c) I think Rise of Furax looks far, far lovelier than my lousy primordial hypermedia confection and d) it is a legally distinct creation. That unfinished HyperCard concept never left the confines of a Macintosh Performa that is even now rusting on a riverbed. If only I'd pitched it somewhere, I'd probably be a MILLIONAIRE by now. A million pounds is still a lot of money, right? Anyway, here's a teaser video for Rise of Furax.

The plot setup here is thusly: some apocalypse cult is raising havoc on three islands off the coast of Rivelune. Five heroes – a snake minstrel, a rhino barbarian, a badger knight, a goat sorcerer and… whatever the hell critter that monk is - have been sent to investigate the whole "world is ending" sheebang and do a little levelling.

As in the very first Might and Magic, you steer the party as one, moving around a grid map. Combat is turn-based and there are "secrets, puzzles, and hidden items everywhere". Also schmürpfs. These confuse me even more than the monk character. They look like angry green omelettes. Any pointers? I googled the word and the closest match I could find was Swiss footballer Pascal Schürpf, who appears neither green nor egg-based.

"Every element, from sprites to textures, was hand-drawn on paper," promises the Steam page. It's out April 2027. There's no demo as yet nor even a proper trailer, but god I enjoyed looking at this, in a week otherwise full of screenshots of, like, suggestive scallion distribution in GTA 6. I should finish that HyperCard game. I still remember which river I threw the Performa into.

A new trailer for Avengers: Doomsday is here, and Marvel fans are convinced that Thor is about to lose his arm and become his comic book counterpart Unworthy Thor.

In one brief scene, Thor's arm is seemingly zapped by Doctor Doom... and appears to catch on fire. We don't see what happens after this, of course, but it's enough to make fans speculate as to whether Thor is going to lose his arm and gain a metal prosthetic, much like he does in Jason Aaron's Unworthy Thor comic book run.

It's worth noting that, in the trailer, Thor's arm is hit between his shoulder and his wrist. This is the same way his arm is severed by Malekith in the comics. Aaron's 2014-2015 Thor run then brings us to The Unworthy Thor, which sees the God of Thunder donning a new arm made of special Black Metal.

Now, other fans have pointed out that this arm-on-fire scene appears to be an extension of the scene in the woods, which we see in the trailer, and think Thor is simply kneeling on the ground and "charging up with divine power." Other fans think the scene is edited to conceal what really happened to his arm. We'll find out soon enough!

Ho ho ho, the RPS Advent Calendar 2026 is... not ready yet. We haven’t written the words, and I keep forgetting to unblur that new picture of Horace (drawn by the reliably talented Amanda Flagg). You, the reader, take a guess at the 24 games we’ve chosen to hide behind Horace’s wall of advent doors this year, finalising your list before the calendar launches on December 1st. Once all games are revealed, those with the most accurate guesses shall bask forever in the glory of their triumph, and also bag some free access to the RPS Supporter programme. 3rd place wins a three-month subscription, 2nd place wins six months, and the 1st place Guesser Supreme wins a full year of Supp perks.

Be warned, though, that victory will demand a sharp mind and an impeccable memory. Or, at the very least, a willingness to go back through our reviews and What Are We Playing This Weekend posts, to remind yourself which games have taken our fancies these past twelve months. Anecdotally, I think we’ve been slightly better at actually writing about our favourites in 2026 than we were for last year’s calendar, which should hopefully make for an easier Guessing Game. If also, perhaps, a more competitive one?

You can read up on the full game eligibility rules, start discussing your picks, and submit your guesses by joining the #2026-advent-calendar-guessing-game channel in the RPS Discord linked above. Note that you don’t need to correctly guess the position of an included game to earn a point for it, only its presence in the list, though you should specify which game you think will earn the coveted Day 24 door – our overall top game of the year, essentially – as this detail will serve as one of the tiebreakers in the event of a draw.

Thanks again to Aerothorn for setting this up, and good luck to all who participate! Here’s one hint, for free: we didn’t have Sin, Oisin, and Jeremy P voting for the Advent Calendar after having them for the RPS 100, so don’t rely too much on the latter for inspiration. Sorry, Unbeatable.

#3625. UK Prime Minister won't be playing GTA 6, government says, while hailing Rockstar Games a "British success story"

Grand Theft Auto 6's seismic launch has registered on a governmental level. A spokesperson for UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has hailed the game as a "British success story", but confirmed Burnham himself won't be playing it. His diary is apparently "very full".

"Rockstar Games is a British success story made in Edinburgh," a Downing Street spokesperson told The Independent - referencing the series' Scottish origins and ongoing development at Rockstar North - "and many fans are already saying GTA has been worth the wait." When asked if Burnham will be making time for GTA 6, the spokesperson responded: "His diary is very full. He won't be playing it."

Downing Street went on to address the issue of teenagers potentially skipping school to play the game, emphasising that children "should be in classrooms" this week because "every day in school matters".

The leader of Labour's opposition, the Conservative party's Kemi Badendoch, recently expressed similar concerns. "I know people are worried about the game content," she wrote. "At the same time, I'd be more worried about a kid who played it all day, who was in their bedroom all day, than one who spends half-an-hour on it and then went out and did something else."

GTA 6's culture-shaking success was unlikely to pass without reference by the government, but the celebratory tone is a marked departure from Burnham's predecessor Kier Starmer calling Rockstar's firing of 34 staff last year "deeply concerning". We are awaiting a verdict in the resulting employment tribunal related to it.

This state recognition of GTA 6 is not without precedent. It wasn't long ago that French President Emmanuel Macron congratulated Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 on its award-winning and heart-winning success. That game sold 8 million copies in one year; GTA 6 is estimated to have sold 25 million copies in one day.

GTA 6 has been hailed as a generational release - an exorbitantly luxurious game that "pushes back the horizon of video games", Chris Tapsell wrote in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.
